Class TaskService

java.lang.Object
de.hallerweb.enterprise.prioritize.service.project.TaskService
@Service @Transactional public class TaskService extends Object
Manages tasks on a project's Blackboard. Authorization is delegated to ProjectService: any manager or member of the owning project may work on its tasks.
Author:
peter haller

    • createScheduledTask

      public Task createScheduledTask(Project project, String name, String description, int priority)
      Creates a task from a recurring schedule's template on project's blackboard with status TaskStatus.CREATED. This is a trusted system path invoked by the scheduler, not a user: it performs no membership check, mirroring the user-less ingest paths (MQTT / telemetry). It stays decoupled from the scheduling model — the caller unpacks the template.
      Parameters:
      project - the owning project (its blackboard receives the task)
      name - the generated task's name
      description - the generated task's description
      priority - the generated task's priority
      Returns:
      the persisted task

    • updateWorkSession

      public TaskService.WorkSession updateWorkSession(Long taskId, Long sessionId, Instant from, Instant until, String reason, PUser user)
      Corrects the bounds of a completed work session, keeping the originally recorded bounds and recording who changed them and why. The task's status is left alone — a correction is bookkeeping, not a state transition.
      Parameters:
      taskId - the task id
      sessionId - the work session's id (from TaskService.WorkSession.id())
      from - the corrected start, must lie before until
      until - the corrected end, must not lie in the future
      reason - why the session is being changed, required
      user - the requesting user (project manager, or a participant of this session)
      Returns:
      the corrected session
      Throws:
      NoSuchElementException - if no such completed session exists on the task
      IllegalStateException - if the session is still running
      IllegalArgumentException - if the reason is missing or the bounds are not plausible

    • addWorkSession

      public TaskService.WorkSession addWorkSession(Long taskId, Instant from, Instant until, String reason, Long forUserId, PUser user)
      Books a work session that was never clocked at all — someone forgot to scan on arrival. The session is marked TaskService.CorrectionKind.MANUAL_ENTRY: there is no recorded state to preserve, so it is visible as hand-entered for good.
      Parameters:
      taskId - the task id
      from - the session's start, must lie before until
      until - the session's end, must not lie in the future
      reason - why the session is being added, required
      forUserId - the user the time is booked for; null books it for the requesting user. Booking someone else's time is reserved for the project manager.
      user - the requesting user (must be manager or member)
      Returns:
      the newly booked session
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the reason is missing or the bounds are not plausible

    • stopTrackingAt

      public Task stopTrackingAt(Long taskId, Instant until, String reason, Long targetUserId, PUser user)
      Stops a running session with an earlier timestamp than now — the "forgot to clock out last night, noticed this morning" case. Unlike stopTracking(Long, PUser), this records who shortened the session and why; the start is left untouched.
      Parameters:
      taskId - the task id
      until - when the work actually ended; after the session's start, not in the future
      reason - why the session is being closed retroactively, required
      targetUserId - whose clock to close; null means the caller's own. Closing someone else's is a manager job (enforced via the correction rights).
      user - the requesting user (project manager, or a participant of this session)
      Returns:
      the updated task
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if that user has no clock running on this task
      IllegalArgumentException - if the reason is missing or until is not plausible

    • startEquipmentUsage

      public Task startEquipmentUsage(Long taskId, Long resourceId, PUser user)
      Clocks a piece of equipment onto a task, opening an TimeSpan.TimeSpanType.EQUIPMENT_USAGE span at the current server time.

      Refuses if the device is already clocked in anywhere — including on another task. A device is in one place at a time, so a second start means someone forgot to clock it out at the last job; silently moving it would turn that mistake into plausible-looking data.

      Parameters:
      taskId - the task id
      resourceId - the equipment to clock in
      user - the requesting user (must be manager or member)
      Returns:
      the updated task
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if this device already has a clock running, here or elsewhere

    • stopEquipmentUsageAt

      public Task stopEquipmentUsageAt(Long taskId, Long resourceId, Instant until, String reason, PUser user)
      Clocks a piece of equipment off with an earlier timestamp than now, recording who shortened the booking and why. The device case of "forgot to clock out", which is the normal case rather than the exception: nobody walks back to the lift at knock-off time to scan it.

      Unlike a work session, this needs no ownership check beyond project membership — a device has no session of its own to protect, and whoever notices the running clock is rarely the manager. The audit trail still records who did it.

      Parameters:
      taskId - the task id
      resourceId - the equipment to clock out
      until - when the device actually stopped; after the booking's start, not in the future
      reason - why the booking is being closed retroactively, required
      user - the requesting user (must be manager or member)
      Returns:
      the updated task
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if this device is not clocked in on this task
      IllegalArgumentException - if the reason is missing or until is not plausible

    • addEquipmentSession

      public TaskService.EquipmentSession addEquipmentSession(Long taskId, Long resourceId, Instant from, Instant until, String reason, PUser user)
      Books an equipment usage that was never clocked at all - the lift stood on site all day and nobody scanned it. The booking is created closed and marked TaskService.CorrectionKind.MANUAL_ENTRY, so it stays visible as hand-entered.

      The device's current rate is stamped on it just as it is when a booking is clocked out normally: without the stamp the booking would appear in getEquipmentCost(Long, PUser) as unpriced, and the job's total would quietly be too low.

      Parameters:
      taskId - the task id
      resourceId - the equipment the booking is about
      from - when the device arrived, must lie before until
      until - when it left, must not lie in the future
      reason - why the booking is being added, required
      user - the requesting user (must be manager or member)
      Returns:
      the newly booked usage
      Throws:
      NoSuchElementException - if the task or the resource does not exist
      IllegalArgumentException - if the reason is missing or the bounds are not plausible

    • updateEquipmentSession

      public TaskService.EquipmentSession updateEquipmentSession(Long taskId, Long sessionId, Instant from, Instant until, String reason, PUser user)
      Corrects the bounds of a completed equipment booking, keeping the bounds as first recorded and noting who changed them and why.

      The rate stamped on the booking is deliberately left untouched. It records what the device cost while it was on the job; re-stamping it during a correction in December would reprice work done in March at today's rate - precisely what the stamp was introduced to prevent. A booking that carries no stamp keeps none: a rate cannot be invented afterwards.

      Parameters:
      taskId - the task id
      sessionId - the booking's id (from TaskService.EquipmentSession.id())
      from - the corrected start, must lie before until
      until - the corrected end, must not lie in the future
      reason - why the booking is being changed, required
      user - the requesting user (must be manager or member)
      Returns:
      the corrected booking
      Throws:
      NoSuchElementException - if no such completed booking exists on the task
      IllegalStateException - if the booking is still running
      IllegalArgumentException - if the reason is missing or the bounds are not plausible

    • deleteEquipmentSession

      public void deleteEquipmentSession(Long taskId, Long sessionId, PUser user)
      Removes a completed equipment booking - the wrong device was scanned, or the booking belongs to another job entirely. Project manager only: deleting takes the booking's audit trail and its cost line with it, and the log line below is all that remains of it.
      Parameters:

      sessionId - the booking's id
      user - the requesting user (must be the project manager)
      Throws:
      NoSuchElementException - if no such completed booking exists on the task
      IllegalStateException - if the booking is still running

    • getEquipmentCost

      @Transactional(readOnly=true) public TaskService.EquipmentCostReport getEquipmentCost(Long taskId, PUser user)
      Returns what the equipment on this task has cost so far: duration times the rate each booking was closed at, plus totals per currency. Running bookings count live up to now, so the figure for a device still on site is provisional by nature. Manager or member.

      One line per device and rate: a device booked before and after a price change appears twice, once at each rate. See accumulate(Map, Task, TimeSpan, long, Instant).

      Parameters:
      taskId - the task id
      user - the requesting user
      Returns:
      the cost report, with empty lines when no equipment was ever booked

    • getLabourCost

      @Transactional(readOnly=true) public TaskService.LabourCostReport getLabourCost(Long taskId, PUser user)
      What the work booked on this task cost, grouped by qualification level and never by person.

      Project manager only. Not member, not admin: these figures are the wage structure of a business seen from the side, and the person accountable for a job's calculation is the one running it. The same reasoning as everywhere else in the project authorization model — an administrator who needs this takes the project over first, which is a visible act.

      Parameters:
      taskId - the task id
      user - the requesting user (must be the project manager)
      Returns:
      the labour cost report, with empty lines when nothing was ever tracked

    • getTaskCost

      @Transactional(readOnly=true) public TaskService.TaskCostReport getTaskCost(Long taskId, PUser user)
      What the task cost altogether: the equipment block, the labour block, and one total per currency across both. Project manager only, for the same reason as getLabourCost(Long, PUser).
      Parameters:
      taskId - the task id
      user - the requesting user (must be the project manager)
      Returns:
      both blocks and the combined totals
